Hi Max / Lina —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same record and clear next steps. Feel free to correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes during peak trading hours (08:00–11:00 PT), causing customer-facing features to exceed 350ms P95 target.
- Cost per inference is unpredictable with current self-hosted setup; need unit economics to plan for scale.
- Regulatory constraint: logs and prompt data must remain in US region and be retained for 12 months.

Goals you described:
- Achieve P95 generation latency <= 200ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) and <= 400ms for long responses (~512 tokens) under target concurrency.
- Support sustained throughput of ~120 prompts/sec (short-form) with occasional bursts to 300 TPS for short-form with queuing/circuit-breakers.
- Maintain privacy controls: no ephemeral KV leaks; support customer-managed KMS for private deployment.

Technical constraints we noted:
- Primary model family: 7B-13B dense and a potential 70B quantized variant for high-quality reasoning.
- Average tokenization length per request: 60 tokens (short) and up to 450 tokens (long).
- Current infra: mixed GPU fleet (V100 / A100 older gen) on prem; open to dedicated cloud capacity.

Attachments I promised to share:
- kraken_latency_matrix.xlsx (we'll populate with a baseline latency matrix and sequence-length buckets)
- redwood_deploy_topology.pdf (high-level options: Hosted API, Dedicated pool, Private VPC)

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Dev (SE): provide a rough latency/throughput sketch for the three topology options (hosted, dedicated, private) with recommended GPU classes and expected P95 estimates. (Dev — by EOD Wednesday)
- Aditya (AE): share preliminary commercial guidance for Dedicated vs Private (ballpark seat/commit ranges). (Aditya — by Friday)
- Kraken: share a small sample of peak hour request distribution and any redaction rules for PII prior to a focused perf run. (Max/Lina — by next Tue)

If that aligns, I'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive with your infra and security folks next week.

Best,

Thanks Naomi — this looks right, appreciate the summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Latency targets: the 200ms P95 for short responses is our ideal; 250ms P95 is acceptable as a first milestone while we tune caching. The 400ms for long responses is a hard ceiling.
2) Throughput: the 120 prompts/sec is for our US web app peak. The 300 TPS burst comes from promotional email drops — those can be queued if needed but we'd like a graceful degraded experience rather than timeouts.

4) Security: SOC2 attestation on the vendor side is required for procurement sign-off, and we need proof of KMS integration options.

Thanks Naomi / Lina — taking the SE lane here with a compact technical sketch and trade-offs per topology. I'll use the sample numbers you provided and make conservative latency/throughput estimates. This is intended as a starting point for the deep-dive.

Assumptions
- Short request: 60 tokens (input+output), long request: 450 tokens.
- Serving model options: 7B float32/8-bit quant (fastest), 13B 4-bit quant (balanced), 70B 4-bit quant (high quality, higher latency).
- Target concurrency: steady 120 RPS short; burst to 300 RPS short for ~5–10m windows.

Option A — Hosted Redwood API (multitenant, auto-scaling)
- Recommended profile: A100-equivalent GPU pool, dynamic batching, KV prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Expected P95 (short): 120–160ms (with batching turned on and small max batch window).
- Expected P95 (long): 250–350ms depending on beam/temperature settings.
- Burst handling: autoscale + prewarmed workers; 300 TPS bursts likely need short queueing (100–300ms) unless you provision burst capacity.
- Pros: fastest to start, minimal ops, good for initial validation.
- Cons: less control over private KMS and strict data residency unless using our Dedicated/Private mode.

Option B — Dedicated GPU Pool (reserved capacity for Kraken)
- Recommended profile: mixture of 8x A100-80GB (for 70B) + 16x A10/A100-40GB (for 7B/13B).
- Expected P95 (short): 90–160ms depending on pinned kernels and batch sizing.
- Expected P95 (long): 220–330ms.
- Burst handling: predictable throughput up to the provisioned capacity; cheaper per-token at scale.
- Pros: better economic predictability, can be colocated in the US region only, supports customer-managed KMS options.
- Cons: commit required; longer lead time to activate (2–4 weeks provisioning).

Option C — Private VPC / On-prem-ish (customer-managed infra)
- Recommended profile: customers provide GPU fleet (A100/A40 mix); Redwood control plane runs in your VPC.
- Expected P95 (short): highly dependent on hardware sizing—if using equivalent A100 fleet expect similar numbers to Dedicated.
- Pros: maximum control for compliance; full KMS/HSM integration; logs stay in your network.
- Cons: ops overhead and slower iteration.

Performance knobs and SLO controls
- KV prefix caching for repeat prompts can reduce mean latency by 20–45% for short flows.
- Dynamic batching: tune max batch size to keep P95 under 250ms for short requests.
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization on 13B typically cuts latency by ~30–40% vs float while preserving quality; 70B quant will still be ~2x slower than 13B quant at similar token lengths.
- Autoscaling policy: use a combination of CPU queue depth and token/sec triggers; add a circuit-breaker that falls back to a cheaper model variant for non-critical traffic.

Immediate technical asks from Kraken for a focused perf run
1) Sample peak-hour request histogram (Lina to share).
2) A representative prompt set (5–10 short and long prompts) and expected quality thresholds.
3) Any network egress constraints and IP allowlists for a perf window.

Proposed next steps
- I'll prepare a two-page technical note with expected P95/P99 numbers per topology and a cost delta summary (tokens/sec cost) by Friday.
- Naomi / Aditya: we can use that note to align on commercial and scheduling for a perf-run.

If useful I can also include a small synthetic run (hosted sandbox) to show baseline numbers for the 7B/13B quant variants prior to any dedicated provisioning.

Cheers,
